If you turn on smart scan, the photo you scan is sent to an online text-reading service (OCR.space) to read the label. The app shows ads from Google AdMob, which may use your device's advertising ID; your saved medicines are never used for ads.

legal.termsIntro: Please read these terms before using MedScan. By using the app you agree to them.
legal.privacyIntro: MedScan is built to keep your information on your device. This policy explains what the app handles and why.

terms.s1b: By installing or using MedScan you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.
terms.s2b: MedScan reads the printed text on medicine packaging, lets you review and correct it, and keeps a personal list of the medicines you save, with reminders for the expiry dates printed on them.
terms.s3b: MedScan is not a medical device and gives no medical advice. It does not identify medicines, check doses, check interactions or say whether a medicine is safe to use. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions and check the package itself.
terms.s4t: 4. No diagnosis, recommendations or emergency use
terms.s4b: MedScan does not diagnose conditions, recommend treatments, suggest alternative medicines or give lifestyle advice. It must not be used in an emergency. If someone may have taken the wrong medicine or too much of one, call your local emergency number or a poison control service straight away.
terms.s5b: Text recognition can make mistakes with names, strengths, batch numbers and dates. The app shows what it read so that you can review it, and it never guesses a value for you. You are responsible for checking every saved detail against the original package.
terms.s6b: Expiry reminders are a convenience only. They depend on your device allowing notifications and background activity, so a reminder may arrive late or not at all. Do not rely on them as your only way of checking dates.
terms.s7b: The photos and details you save belong to you and stay on your device. You can edit or delete them at any time. You are responsible for the content you add.
terms.s8b: Use the app only for lawful, personal record keeping. Do not try to copy, reverse engineer or interfere with the app, or use it in a way that could harm you or others.
terms.s9b: The app is provided as it is, without promises that it will be error free or always available. To the extent the law allows, the publisher is not liable for any loss or harm that comes from relying on the app, including from a missed or incorrect reminder or a misread label.
terms.s10b: These terms may be updated from time to time. The date at the top shows when they last changed. Continuing to use the app after an update means you accept the new terms.
terms.s11b: For questions about these terms, please use the contact details on the app's store page.

privacy.s1b: There is no account and no sign-in. Your saved medicine details stay on your device. Photos are read on your device unless you turn on smart scan, which sends only the photo you scan to an online text-reading service (OCR.space). MedScan shows ads from Google AdMob; see section 8.
privacy.s2b: Photos of medicine packaging you take or choose, the text read from them, the details you type or confirm (name, strength, batch, manufacturer, dates), and your settings such as theme and language.
privacy.s3b: Text is read on your device. The details are kept so you can see your medicines and be reminded before the printed expiry dates. They are not used for anything else.
privacy.s4b: Text on a photo is read on your device unless you turn on smart scan. With smart scan, the photo you scan is sent to the online text-reading service OCR.space, only to read the text on it. To show general information about a medicine, only its name (no photo, no personal details) is sent to public health information services: U.S. FDA (openFDA), the U.S. National Library of Medicine (RxNorm, MedlinePlus, DailyMed) and Wikipedia. Results are kept on your device for offline use.
privacy.s5b: Everything is stored in the app's private storage on your device. Deleting a medicine removes its record and its image. Uninstalling the app removes all of its data.
privacy.s6b: Your data sits in the app's private storage and is protected by your device's own security, such as the screen lock and device encryption. Anyone who can unlock your phone could open the app, so keep your device locked.
privacy.s7b: Camera: only to take a photo when you ask. Photos and files: only to open an image you choose. Notifications: only to remind you about expiry dates. You can turn any of these off in your device settings.
privacy.s8b: The app does not send your medicine records anywhere. It shows ads served by Google AdMob. To show and measure ads, Google may use your device's advertising ID and similar device and usage information, and where the law requires it you are asked for your choice first. Ads are never based on your saved medicines, and you can reset or limit the advertising ID in your device settings. The app may also download its typeface from Google Fonts the first time it runs; your device's network address is visible to those services.
privacy.s9b: MedScan does not sell or share your medicine records. Ads are provided by Google AdMob under Google's own privacy policy. If your phone's own backup feature is on, the operating system may include the app's data in your device backup, under your own account and settings.
privacy.s10b: The app is meant for adults managing medicines. A parent or guardian should manage the app for a child.
privacy.s11b: If this policy changes, the date at the top will change and the new text will appear here.

notes.title: Important notes
notes.rx: A doctor's prescription is required before use. Do not self-medicate.
notes.pharmacist: Tell your doctor or pharmacist about allergies, pregnancy, other medicines and existing health conditions.
notes.leaflet: Follow the dose and instructions on your prescription and the leaflet inside the pack.
notes.expired: Do not use a medicine that is expired, damaged or has been stored incorrectly.
notes.keep: Keep out of reach of children and never share your medicines.
notes.emergency: Get urgent medical help for a severe reaction, an allergic reaction or an overdose.
